name: Minshina's Skull
summary: In Sen'jin Village, Master Gadrin hears his dead brother Minshina's desperate cries. Zalazane slew Minshina on the Echo Isles and bound his spirit to his severed skull. You can free him from torment by reclaiming the skull from Zalazane's ritual grounds.

sections.title: A Plea from the Shadows
sections.body: Master Gadrin is one of the Darkspear tribe's spiritual anchors in Sen'jin Village. Yet dark visions torment him. His brother Minshina fell when Zalazane betrayed the tribe and seized the Echo Isles. Minshina died in the conflict, but death brought him no peace. Troll tradition and voodoo mysticism hold that a spirit can remain bound after the body dies. Now Minshina's tormented voice reaches Gadrin in his dreams, pleading to be saved from a fate worse than death.

sections.title: Zalazane's Circle of Power
sections.body: Zalazane does more than kill his former brethren. He traps their souls to fuel his dark sorcery. He bound Minshina's spirit to his own skull, now set in a circle of power on the largest of the Echo Isles. Hexed trolls guard the circle as candles burn through the rites. The skull focuses Zalazane's twisted mojo. While it remains there, Minshina is captive to the witch doctor's will.

sections.title: Freedom in Death
sections.body: To free Minshina, you cross east from Sen'jin Village to the southern Echo Isles. You break into the ritual ring and take the skull from Zalazane's grasp. When you return Minshina's remains to Master Gadrin, the dark bindings break. Minshina's grateful spirit briefly appears and bows in reverence. Then he leaves for the realm of the ancestors.

faq.answer: Minshina was Master Gadrin's brother. Zalazane murdered him during the uprising on the Echo Isles, then defiled his remains with dark sorcery.

faq.q: Why is Minshina's spirit trapped in his skull?
faq.answer: Zalazane uses dark voodoo and warlock magic to enslave the spirits of slain Darkspear trolls. He bound Minshina's soul to his physical skull and placed it in a circle of power. This denied Minshina passage to the afterlife and let Zalazane harness his spirit.

faq.q: Where is the circle of power located?
faq.answer: The circle of power lies atop a hill on the southernmost and largest of the Echo Isles, off Durotar's southeastern coast. Ritual candles, dancing hexed trolls, and displays of skulls mark the site.

faq.q: What happens when the skull is brought back to Sen'jin Village?
faq.answer: When Master Gadrin receives the skull, the necromantic bindings shatter. Minshina's ghostly form appears before Gadrin and you, bows in gratitude, then vanishes to rest peacefully with the ancestors.

faq.q: Who is Zalazane and why did he do this?
faq.answer: Zalazane was once a respected Darkspear witch doctor. Driven mad by lust for power, he turned on his tribe and used hexes to mind-control his brothers and sisters. He drove the remaining Darkspear refugees onto Durotar's mainland.

faq.q: Why can't Gadrin retrieve the skull himself?
faq.answer: Master Gadrin cannot leave Sen'jin Village unprotected. He holds the settlement together, guides the young Darkspear leadership, advises chieftain Vol'jin, and works to counter Zalazane's expanding hexes along the coast.

angles.text: As a Darkspear troll, you honor family and tribe by recovering Minshina's skull. You strike at Zalazane's corruption of ancestral voodoo traditions.
As a priest, you know the sanctity of a departed soul and the horror of ritual necromancy that keeps a fallen brother from eternal peace.
As a shaman, you revere the spirits of the ancestors. Breaking Zalazane's circle releases a tortured soul and restores balance between the spirit world and the living.
As a member of the Horde, you honor its bond with the Darkspear tribe by helping Master Gadrin. Your aid proves an ally's grief is shared by all.
